evidence.claim: In 1799, the First Great Western Turnpike Corporation received a charter to build from Albany to Cherry Valley; a second company was chartered in 1803 to extend the road to Cazenovia.
evidence.quote: The First Great Western Turnpike Corporation was chartered in 1799 to build a road from Albany, the capital of New York, to the Revolutionary War frontier town of Cherry Valley. In 1803, a second corporation, the Third Great Western Turnpike, was chartered to further extend the road to Cazenovia.

evidence.claim: Together, the two turnpikes became a stagecoach route in 1816.
evidence.quote: The two turnpikes, collectively known as the Cherry Valley Turnpike, became a stagecoach route in 1816.

evidence.claim: Competition from the Erie Canal and the Utica and Schenectady Railroad reduced the turnpike’s revenue. It ceased collecting tolls in 1857, before the automobile era brought its later touring trade.
evidence.quote: The establishment of the Erie Canal and the Utica and Schenectady Railroad slowly ate away at the revenues of the Cherry Valley Turnpike. The turnpike stopped being a toll road in 1857.
